newJerseyStatePrograms.name: Tuition Aid Grant (TAG)
newJerseyStatePrograms.eligibility: Need-based. The student must be a New Jersey resident for at least 12 consecutive months immediately before enrollment. For a dependent student, the student and parents must meet that residency rule, or the student must have graduated from a NJ high school after attending it for at least 3 years. The student must show financial need and be a citizen, an eligible non-citizen, or eligible to file the NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application. The student must enroll full-time in an approved program at an approved NJ institution and maintain satisfactory academic progress. There is no fixed income cap: the award depends on the New Jersey Eligibility Index (NJEI), which HESAA calculates from the aid application. At public research universities the award is $0 once the NJEI reaches 9,500. At independent colleges it is $0 once the NJEI is over 10,499.
newJerseyStatePrograms.award: 2026-27 full-time awards, applied to tuition only. Public research universities (Rutgers, NJIT): $2,396 to $10,964, depending on NJEI. HESAA states that the actual award may be higher than the table value, based on the institution's tuition, but may not exceed tuition. Independent colleges (Stevens): $2,176 to $14,404, depending on NJEI.
newJerseyStatePrograms.application: FAFSA, or the NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application for NJ Dreamers, then complete the State grant record in NJFAMS
newJerseyStatePrograms.deadline: 2026-27, new students and high school seniors: the FAFSA or NJ Alternative application must be processed by September 15, 2026 for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027, and the State record in NJFAMS must be completed by October 1, 2026. For Spring 2027 only: application by February 15, 2027 and NJFAMS record by March 1, 2027. Renewal applicants: April 15, 2026. The 2027-28 deadlines were not found.

newJerseyStatePrograms.name: Garden State Guarantee (GSG)
newJerseyStatePrograms.eligibility: Need-based. Family adjusted gross income (AGI) must be between $0 and $65,000; a negative AGI is not eligible. For a dependent student, only the parents' AGI counts. The student must be a NJ resident enrolled full-time (at least 12 credits per semester) at an in-state public four-year institution and working toward a first bachelor's degree. Funding goes only to third-year students (60-89 accumulated credits) and fourth-year students (90-128 credits). First-year and second-year students are not eligible.
newJerseyStatePrograms.award: Pays the tuition and approved educational fees that other grants do not already cover, for a net price of $0 in tuition and fees. Paid for up to 4 semesters or until the student reaches 128 credits, whichever comes first.
newJerseyStatePrograms.application: Automatic consideration after filing the FAFSA or the NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application
newJerseyStatePrograms.deadline: Same State deadlines as TAG (for 2026-27, the application must be processed by September 15, 2026)

newJerseyStatePrograms.name: NJ STARS (and NJ STARS II)
newJerseyStatePrograms.eligibility: Merit. The student must be a NJ resident ranked in the top 15.0% of the high school class at the end of junior or senior year. The student must enroll full-time at their home county college. NJ STARS II is for NJ STARS recipients who earn an associate degree with a cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher and have family income under $250,000; it pays toward transferring to a TAG-participating four-year college.
newJerseyStatePrograms.award: NJ STARS pays tuition only, after State and federal grants are subtracted, for up to 5 semesters and up to 18 credits per semester, at the county college. It does not pay for a first year at a four-year college.
newJerseyStatePrograms.application: Apply for admission to the home county college, file the FAFSA or NJ Alternative application within State deadlines, and complete the State record in NJFAMS
newJerseyStatePrograms.deadline: Same State deadlines as TAG (September 15, 2026 for the application; October 1, 2026 for the NJFAMS record)

newJerseyStatePrograms.name: Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF)
newJerseyStatePrograms.eligibility: The student must come from an educationally and economically disadvantaged background and be a NJ resident for 12 consecutive months before the award. The 2026-27 gross income limit for a household of 4 is $64,300, with an asset cap of $12,860 (household of 1: $31,300; add $11,000 for each additional family member). Each college runs its own EOF admission process, and spaces are limited.
newJerseyStatePrograms.award: $200 to $3,050 per year for undergraduates, depending on the type of institution and financial need, plus support services such as counseling and tutoring
newJerseyStatePrograms.application: File the FAFSA and apply through the EOF office at the college, following that college's own admission process
newJerseyStatePrograms.deadline: Each college sets its own EOF deadline; the State site gives none

newJerseyStatePrograms.name: Governor's Urban Scholarship (GUS)
newJerseyStatePrograms.eligibility: Merit and need. The student must rank in the top 5.0% of the class with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher at the end of junior year. The student must live in a designated high-need community at the time of high school nomination and have an NJEI below 10,500. The student must be a NJ resident for 12 consecutive months and enroll full-time at an eligible NJ college.
newJerseyStatePrograms.award: The published material gives no dollar amount; the award depends on annual State appropriations
newJerseyStatePrograms.application: No application. The high school reports its top 15% to HESAA, which notifies eligible students in December of senior year. The student must also file the FAFSA or NJ Alternative application each year within State deadlines.

newJerseyGrantsPortable: No. New Jersey state grants such as TAG, GSG, EOF and GUS can be used only at approved New Jersey colleges, so they do not follow a student to an out-of-state college.
